question: How many port calls will IMF PortWatch record at Ukraine's three main Black Sea ports over the latest reported week as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Resolution depends only on what PortWatch prints, and I queried the resolving layer directly (ArcGIS Daily_Ports_Data, ISO3='UKR'; max date 2026-09-11, matching HDX's stated 'data to 11 Sep 2026, updated 16 Sep 2026'). Reference class = 7-day sums of this same series in its post-October-2024 regime: 21 port calls across 700 days (2024-10-12 to 2026-09-11), every non-zero day exactly 1, implying ~0.21 per 7-day window and P(0)~0.82. The regime break is an instrument artifact, not the war: the same three ports logged 2,143 calls in 2024 (205-265/month Jan-Sep) and then 9 in all of 2025 and 9 in 2026 YTD, while Ukraine's corridor was demonstrably moving large volumes in 2025. That decoupling is the crux: news of the 22 July 2026 halt, the 92% grain-carrier drop, or a Turkish-brokered maritime truce cannot raise a counter that already ignored two years of real traffic. Adjusting slightly down from the 2-year base rate for the current deeper halt (zero calls for 49 straight days through 11 Sep) and slightly up for model risk, I get P(0)~0.84, P(1)~0.13, P(2)~0.02, P(>=3)~0.01. The window will cover ~19-25 Sep (or 12-18 Sep if the 29 Sep refresh slips) - either way inside the flat-zero regime. Main residual risk is a PortWatch reprocessing/geofence repair, absent for 23 months; even a repair with traffic down ~90% would land in low single digits, so >60 needs repair AND full normalization inside ten days - priced at 0.5%. No prediction market prices this or any near-miss contract.

- No foreign cargo vessel entered a Greater Odesa port from ~20-22 Jul 2026; ~90% of operators suspended calls after 57 strikes on vessels and 67 on port infrastructure (OSW, 28 Jul 2026).

- Greater Odesa port terminals handled 11.2 thousand tonnes of grain in 1-15 Sep 2026, down 77.6% month-on-month; 82% of rail-carried export grain went via western land crossings instead (USM/Spike Brokers, Sep 2026).
- Russia rejected Turkey's 8 Aug 2026 Black Sea moratorium proposal on 14 Aug 2026 ('no grounds for half-measures', Dep. FM Grushko); no arrangement in force as of 21 Sep 2026.
- Near-daily strikes on cargo vessels, tankers and OSVs around Yuzhny and Odesa continued 31 Aug - 6 Sep 2026 (Palaemon Maritime security report).
- Ukrainian Ports Association (Barinov, Kyiv Post, 21 Sep 2026): strikes since Jul 2026 target civilian commercial vessels; 300+ vessels and 1,000+ infrastructure elements damaged since 2022.
- Ukrainian Agrarian Council advised exporters to plan on deep-water port operations not resuming before December/January.
- Ukraine cut its 2026/27 grain export forecast to 38-40 Mt from 43 Mt, citing attacks on the Odesa hub.

EVIDENCE TOWARD HIGHER ACTIVITY:
- Ukrainian officials state the ports remain legally open; suspension is each operator's commercial decision, so it can reverse without any government act.
- Reports of a Kyiv-run temporary corridor still moving occasional vessels in September 2026, with some cargoes lifted from Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi.
- Turkey, plus SAMSIAD and regional business groups (21 Sep 2026), pressing for a 'Black Sea Safe Trade Corridor', international insurance mechanisms and an early-warning centre; wheat futures eased mid-Sep on renewed ceasefire hopes.
- One trade projection cited Greater Odesa operating at ~30% of prewar capacity in September 2026 and ~50% from October.
- Corridor protocol as published requires AIS ON within 5 miles of the northern waiting area and while alongside in port - so detectable calls are not structurally impossible.
- Earlier port-strike waves in late 2025 and early 2026 did not halt operations for long.

The dominant residual risk is on the instrument side, not the war: a PortWatch geofence repair or backfill would jump the reading by an order of magnitude - but absent for 23 months, and with real traffic down ~90% a repaired counter would land in low single digits, so clearing 60 needs repair AND full 2024-style normalization inside ten days. Priced at 0.4%. No human prediction market prices this or any comparable contract.
calls.reconciliation: The runs did not disagree on the instrument's data - all three queried PortWatch's Daily_Ports_Data layer and returned the same series (max date 2026-09-11; monthly 2026 combined totals 2/0/0/2/0/1/4/0/0; every non-zero day exactly 1 since Nov 2024; all rows zero from 25 Jul or 11 Aug through 11 Sep depending on the window each pulled). Factual disputes I settled from the dossiers: (a) publication lag - Run 3's '~10-day' is measured from Now rather than from publication; the background's 'as of 16 Sep, covered through 11 Sep' fixes a 5-day coverage-to-publish lag, so the resolving window is most likely 19-25 Sep with 12-18 Sep as fallback, and both lie wholly inside the flat-zero regime, making the dispute immaterial; (b) 20 vs 21 post-break calls - reconciled as the same count over different start dates (2024-10-12 vs Nov 2024), weekly rate 0.21 either way; (c) 2026 per-port split - Run 1's Pivdennyi 3 / Chornomorsk 3 / Odessa 2 sums to 8, while Run 2's dated list and Run 3 both give Pivdennyi 4, summing to the 9 all three agree on; Run 1's split is the error and the total is unaffected. No web access this run, so I could not independently check the 22 Sep refresh (which may already have landed as of Now, 2026-09-21T17:12Z, though that is a Monday and all runs place refreshes on Tuesday) - that uncertainty is carried in the distribution rather than resolved. The apparent median gap (Run 3's 0.25 vs Runs 1-2's ~0.10) is a percentile-placement convention inside the zero bin, not a disagreement about probability: implied P(0) is 0.81-0.84 across all three. The one live judgment call - whether the post-22-July halt pushes the rate below the 0.21/week base rate - I resolve in favour of yes but only slightly, since the base rate was itself measured over a period when real traffic was high and the instrument still read near zero, meaning most of that 0.21 is detection noise rather than traffic-proportional signal. I carry forward the post-Oct-2024 reference class and a dispersion of ~1.4 counts, which I agree with; my percentiles sit between the runs because the reconciled evidence puts them there, not by averaging.

disagreements.verdict: Agreed by all three and corroborated: 2025 recorded 9 calls while Ukraine's corridor moved record volumes, Q1-2026 container throughput was +43% YoY, and Kpler counted ~15 ships/day into Greater Odesa in July 2026 against PortWatch's 4 for the month. No PortWatch changelog explaining it was found by any run.

disagreements.verdict: Yes, but only slightly. The base rate was measured over a period of high real traffic that the instrument largely missed, so most of it is detection noise; the escalation removes the residual stray-AIS-on stream but cannot subtract much from a counter already near zero. P(0) set at 0.84, at the high end of the runs' 0.81-0.84.

disagreements.claim: Size of the tail above 60 from a PortWatch backfill, geofence repair, or methodology revision
disagreements.verdict: All three priced it at 0.005; I take 0.004. A repair alone lands in low single digits given real traffic down ~90%, so clearing 60 requires repair plus full 2024-style normalization within ten days. No run found any announced revision plan.

disagreements.claim: Whether any prediction market or bookmaker prices this quantity
disagreements.verdict: None found by any run or by the harness. The only PortWatch-sourced contracts are Kalshi/Polymarket Strait of Hormuz transit markets - different chokepoint, field and criteria, so evidence at best, not an anchor. I had no web access to re-verify.
